name: caxton-printed-handbill-ad
description: An English printer posted a printed notice offering his prayer book for sale, among the earliest printed adverts in English.

name: boston-news-letter-first-ad
description: A Boston newspaper ran a paid notice offering an estate for sale, the first advertisement printed in the colonies.

name: quaker-oats-man-trademark
description: A smiling man in a broad-brimmed hat became the registered face of an oatmeal brand, the first cereal trademark.

name: pears-soap-bubbles-ad
description: A soap maker bought a painting of a boy blowing soap bubbles and made it one of the most famous ad images of its age.

name: kodak-you-press-the-button
description: A camera maker promised that anyone could take pictures with a simple box, and the slogan made photography a mass hobby.

name: michelin-man-bibendum
description: A tyre company poster showed a mascot built from stacked tyres raising a glass of nails and glass, creating Bibendum.

name: morton-salt-when-it-rains
description: A salt company's slogan about free-flowing grains in damp weather came with a girl under an umbrella on the blue box.

name: mr-peanut-created
description: A schoolboy's drawing won a contest, and a nut in a top hat, monocle and cane became the face of a snack brand.

name: betty-crocker-created
description: A flour company invented a friendly fictional woman to sign its replies to customers' baking questions.

name: burma-shave-roadside-signs
description: A shaving cream firm posted sets of small rhyming signs along rural highways, each line read in turn by passing drivers.

name: wheaties-first-singing-jingle
description: A vocal quartet sang a breakfast cereal's praises on the radio, widely credited as the first singing commercial.

name: coca-cola-santa-claus-ads
description: An artist painted a warm, jolly, red-suited Father Christmas for a soft drink company, shaping how he is pictured.

name: elsie-the-cow-mascot
description: A dairy company introduced a smiling cartoon cow as its spokes-character, who later became a living celebrity at fairs.

name: smokey-bear-debuts
description: A poster of a bear in a ranger hat urged the public to prevent wildfires, launching a long-running public campaign.

name: a-diamond-is-forever-slogan
description: A copywriter's four-word line for a diamond cartel made engagement rings feel timeless and shaped wedding customs.

name: tony-the-tiger-mascot
description: A cartoon tiger appeared on boxes of sugar-coated flakes and became the best-known cereal mascot in America.

name: marlboro-man-campaign
description: A cigarette brand swapped its gentle image for rugged cowboys on horseback in one of the most successful rebrandings ever.

name: vw-think-small-ad
description: A witty, minimal print ad for a tiny German car broke the rules of big-car advertising and changed the industry.

name: ronald-mcdonald-debuts
description: A clown in a red wig and yellow jumpsuit appeared on local television to sell hamburgers to children.

name: pillsbury-doughboy-debuts
description: A little dough character popped out of a tube of rolls in a TV spot, and a poke in the belly earned a giggle.

name: coke-hilltop-teach-the-world
description: Young people from around the world sang on a hillside about buying the world a soft drink in a landmark TV commercial.

name: i-love-new-york-campaign
description: A heart-shaped logo and jingle promoted tourism to a struggling city and state, and the design spread everywhere.

name: apple-1984-super-bowl-ad
description: A runner hurled a hammer at a giant screen in a dystopian spot by a famous film director launching a personal computer.

name: nike-just-do-it-slogan
description: A three-word slogan from a sportswear company became one of the most recognised taglines in advertising history.

name: got-milk-campaign
description: A dairy campaign showed celebrities with milk moustaches and asked a simple question about the drink.

name: apple-think-different-campaign
description: A tribute to rebels and visionaries, with black-and-white portraits, marked a computer maker's co-founder returning.

name: budweiser-whassup-ad
description: Friends on the phone greeted each other with a drawn-out catchphrase in a beer ad that swept popular culture.

name: dove-evolution-film
description: A short film showed an ordinary woman turned by makeup and digital retouching into a billboard model, going viral online.

name: old-spice-man-your-man-could-smell-like
friendly_name: The Man Your Man Could Smell Like
description: A shirtless actor delivered a rapid, absurd pitch for body wash in a spot that became a viral hit.

name: coinbase-bouncing-qr-code-ad
description: A TV spot showed only a QR code drifting around the screen, and viewers scanned it so fast the website crashed.
